In the small tuition room above the kirana shop in Ramgarh, Trisha's maths test came back with 38 marks. Again.
Her cousin Tarun, home from college, sat beside her. "What went wrong?"
"Silly mistakes."
"Why silly mistakes?"
She thought. "I was hurrying."
"Why hurrying?"
"The last questions were left, and ten minutes."
"Why were they left?"
Trisha flipped back to page one. The first five questions, simple equations, had taken her almost half the time. "Because I'm slow on the beginning part. I check each one three times."
Tarun nodded. "So the problem isn't silly mistakes."
"It's speed on easy questions." She grabbed her rough book. "If I practise those till they're fast, I'll have time at the end."
That week, she did twenty quick equations every evening before dinner.

qa.a: Trisha's maths test came back with 38 marks.

qa.a: She probably felt surprised and a little relieved, finding the real cause was slowness on easy questions, not carelessness.

qa.q: What else could Trisha do in the next test, and why?
qa.a: She could check easy questions once, not three times, and go back to them at the end if time is left.

qa.q: How does Tarun see Trisha's discovery?
qa.a: Tarun is pleased to see her find the deeper cause herself, which is why he just nods and lets her work out the fix.
